cards.title: Welcome to Level 2
cards.body: International healthcare systems expect nurses to perform clinical skills consistently, verbalise safety checks, explain rationales, recognise complications and adapt to local equipment and policies.

bullets.label: Level 2 bridges national nursing preparation
bullets.text: Level 2 bridges national nursing preparation with international expectations — strengthening your ability to integrate assessment, procedural skill, clinical judgement, documentation and structured escalation.

bullets.label: Apply internationally recognised procedural safety standards and adapt to unfamiliar equipment
Integrate assessment findings with procedural decisions and recognise complications
Use structured communication, closed-loop confirmation and professional documentation
Provide culturally safe, person-centred care across diverse clinical environments
Each section builds progressively on the last,
bullets.text: Each section builds progressively on the last, preparing you for NCLEX-style competency assessment and real-world international clinical practice.

bullets.label: Different systems use different equipment,
bullets.text: Different systems use different equipment, terminology and competency processes. Safe adaptation requires orientation, supervised practice and confirmation of competence before independent performance.

bullets.label: Confirm scope, supervision requirements and approved equipment
Covers preparation, technique, infection prevention and documentation
Request orientation for unfamiliar devices — seeking help is professionalism
Inspect for redness, pain, swelling and patency. Apply approved aseptic technique with correct securement and labelling.
Maintain closed systems and correct positioning. Confirm placement before use of enteral tubes.
Assess tissue, exudate, infection risk and surrounding skin. Select prescribed products and evaluate healing.
Infiltration, phlebitis, blockage and displacement require prompt action. Never continue despite warning signs.

cards.title: SECTION 3
cards.body: Integrating Clinical Judgement with Procedural Care

bullets.label: Clinical reasoning applies before, during and after every procedure
Confirm indication; assess patient; delay if high risk
Confirm outcome; assess complications; escalate if needed
Use ISBAR or the approved local framework to
bullets.text: Use ISBAR or the approved local framework to communicate situation, assessment, background and required action clearly and efficiently.

bullets.label: Clinical scenario: During nasogastric tube
bullets.text: Clinical scenario: During nasogastric tube insertion, a patient develops severe coughing and oxygen desaturation. The nurse stops immediately, removes the tube, supports breathing and escalates — rather than completing the task.

bullets.label: The patient's condition determines whether to continue
Pause or stop if deterioration occurs intra-procedure
Evaluate outcomes — did the intervention achieve its purpose?
Use structured escalation for all urgent concerns
Reproduce realistic safety challenges. Errors in simulation become opportunities to improve reasoning and teamwork.
Critical instructions are repeated back and confirmed — especially important in emergencies and team procedures.
Use professional interpreters, adapt to health literacy levels and ask rather than assume patient preferences.
Record indication, assessment, procedure, findings, complications and follow-up. Make current risks and actions clear.
By completing Level 2, you will be able to
bullets.text: By completing Level 2, you will be able to perform and explain essential clinical procedures confidently within international healthcare systems — while responding appropriately to unexpected findings.

bullets.label: International practice requires more than
bullets.text: International practice requires more than memorising steps. You must know when a procedure is indicated, when it should be delayed, what requires escalation and how to evaluate whether the intervention achieved its purpose.

bullets.label: Adapted to international clinical environments, performed complex procedures and applied structured escalation
Core clinical skills, safety reasoning and competency frameworks aligned with international examination expectations
Focus moves to leadership, competency systems and procedural quality improvement in international settings

decks.sourceFile: GNPS Program 10 - Level 2 - Section 1 International Qualified Nurse - Presentation deck.pptx

cards.title: Section 1: Applying International Clinical-Skills Standards
cards.body: International healthcare systems differ in equipment, terminology, documentation, and competency processes. Safe adaptation requires orientation, supervised practice, and confirmed competence before independent performance.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you should be able to:

bullets.label: Relate local procedure policy to broader patient safety principles.
Adapt safely and confidently to unfamiliar clinical equipment.
Demonstrate procedural competence under appropriate supervision.
Verbalise rationales and critical safety points during assessment.

cards.title: Core Concept: Local Policy and Scope
cards.body: What to Review Before Any Procedure

bullets.label: Who is authorised to perform the procedure
What level of supervision is required
Which equipment is approved for use
Previous clinical experience does not replace local credentialing. Always confirm scope before acting independently.

cards.title: Core Concept: Competency Assessment
cards.body: Competence is multidimensional. A checklist supports consistency but does not replace professional judgement.

bullets.label: Equipment, environment, and patient identification checks
Accurate, timely recording of findings and actions
Patient explanation, team reporting, and escalation
In simulation and OSCE-style assessments,
bullets.text: In simulation and OSCE-style assessments, nurses are expected to think aloud — demonstrating not just what they do, but why.

bullets.label: Assessors look for clear articulation of:

cards.title: Core Concept: Safe Adaptation
cards.body: When encountering unfamiliar devices or procedures, seeking orientation and supervised practice is a sign of professionalism — not a weakness.

bullets.label: Recognise when a device or procedure is outside your current experience.
Ask for a formal or informal briefing from a trained colleague or educator.
Complete supervised practice before any independent performance.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Safe Adaptation in Practice

bullets.label: An IQN is asked to programme an infusion device not previously encountered in their home country.
Reviews the local policy on infusion device use
Completes supervised training with a senior nurse
Demonstrates correct programming before independent use
This approach ensures patient safety and confirms professional competence within the local context.

cards.title: NCLEX Connection: Clinical Judgement
cards.body: These principles directly align with the NCLEX-RN Clinical Judgement Measurement Model (CJMM), which tests your ability to recognise, analyse, and act safely.

bullets.label: Nurses who can verbalise their reasoning and
bullets.text: Nurses who can verbalise their reasoning and adapt safely to new environments demonstrate the exact competencies assessed in NCLEX and OSCE examinations.

bullets.label: Always review local procedure policy and authorisation requirements before acting.
Never perform independently without first demonstrating local competence.
Articulate the why behind every critical step — in practice and in assessment.
Seeking help with unfamiliar equipment is professional, not a limitation.

cards.title: Why This Section Matters
cards.body: Complex procedures involving vascular access, urinary catheters, enteral tubes, and advanced wounds carry significant patient safety risks.

bullets.label: Assess the clinical indication for each device
Evaluate the ongoing need for invasive devices

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Carry out complex aseptic care using correct technique
Evaluate invasive devices and access sites for ongoing suitability
Identify device-related complications promptly and accurately
Act on concerns and prevent avoidable healthcare-associated infection

cards.title: Core Concept: Vascular Access Care
cards.body: What to Assess at Every Access Site

bullets.label: Look for redness, swelling, leakage and signs of phlebitis
Confirm the line flushes freely without resistance or pain
Use approved technique; ensure dressing, labelling and date are current
Maintain a closed drainage system at all times
Position the bag below bladder level
Perform meatal hygiene according to local policy
Review catheter necessity at every care episode
Confirm correct placement before each use — never assume
Follow organisational policy for placement verification
Maintain tube security, patency and labelling
Evaluate wound type, tissue bed, exudate level, infection risk and surrounding skin condition
Choose or apply prescribed products based on clinical findings and wound healing stage
Monitor response to treatment and document progress at each dressing change
Each complication requires immediate clinical assessment and action according to policy.
Continuing a procedure despite warning signs may cause serious and avoidable harm to the patient.

cards.title: Clinical Example: IV Infiltration in Practice

bullets.label: During an intravenous infusion, a patient reports burning at the site and the area becomes visibly swollen.
Check every device at the start of care and throughout — do not wait for the patient to report a problem
Prompt cessation and reassessment is always safer than continuing with a compromised device
Every interaction with an invasive device is a potential infection risk — treat it as such
Remove any device that is no longer clinically indicated — the best device is the one not needed

bullets.label: Section 3: Integrating Clinical Judgement with Procedural Care

cards.title: Introduction
cards.body: A clinical procedure should never become a task performed in isolation.

bullets.label: Nurses must decide whether it is safe to
bullets.text: Nurses must decide whether it is safe to proceed, interpret findings, respond to changes, and evaluate the outcome — integrating sound clinical judgement at every stage of care.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you should be able to:

bullets.label: Apply reasoning before, during, and after procedures
Airway, breathing, circulation, and patient safety first
Differentiate expected from unexpected clinical signs
Before initiating any procedure, confirm the
bullets.text: Before initiating any procedure, confirm the clinical indication and assess whether the patient's current condition supports proceeding safely.

bullets.label: Delay and seek review whenever risks outweigh the immediate benefit of proceeding.
Continuous observation is essential throughout any procedure. Monitor for:
Pause or stop immediately if deterioration is observed.
Did the intervention achieve its intended purpose? Reassess the patient's condition against the expected outcome.
Identify early signs of adverse effects or unintended consequences before they escalate.
Document findings accurately and hand over any outstanding concerns to the clinical team.
Use ISBAR or your approved framework to ensure clear, structured communication during escalation:

cards.title: CLINICAL EXAMPLE
cards.body: Nasogastric Tube Insertion: When to Stop

bullets.label: Patient safety always takes priority over task
bullets.text: Patient safety always takes priority over task completion. Recognising deterioration and acting promptly — stopping, supporting, and escalating — reflects competent, patient-centred nursing practice.

bullets.label: This scenario is a common NCLEX-style clinical judgement question. Know when to stop and why.
Sound clinical judgement is not a single moment
bullets.text: Sound clinical judgement is not a single moment — it is a continuous cycle applied before, during, and after every procedure to keep patients safe and care outcomes optimal.

bullets.label: The patient's status determines whether to continue any procedure
Continuous observation is non-negotiable during care
Confirm effectiveness and assess for complications post-procedure
Use ISBAR to communicate urgent concerns clearly and promptly

decks.title: Simulation, Communication and Professional Documentation
decks.sourceFile: GNPS Program 10 - Level 2 - Section 4 International Qualified Nurse - Presentation deck.pptx

cards.title: GNPS Program 10: Mastering Essential Clinical Skills
cards.body: Global Nursing Professional Series · Level 2 – International Qualified Nurse (IQN)

cards.title: What This Section Covers
cards.body: Section 4 equips internationally qualified nurses with the simulation skills, communication frameworks, and documentation standards expected in global clinical practice.

bullets.label: Practise procedures and emergencies in a safe environment
Confirm critical instructions in real-time clinical scenarios
Adapt care to individual needs, language and health literacy
Record procedural care to international clinical standards

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: By the end of this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Participate effectively in simulation exercises and structured debriefing
Apply closed-loop communication during clinical procedures and emergencies
Provide culturally safe explanations and facilitate informed consent
Document procedural care accurately to professional and legal standards
Simulation reproduces realistic clinical safety
bullets.text: Simulation reproduces realistic clinical safety challenges — without exposing real patients to avoidable risk. It allows nurses to practise skills, make decisions under pressure, and refine teamwork.

bullets.label: Errors in simulation are learning
bullets.text: Errors in simulation are learning opportunities, not failures. Structured reflection after each scenario turns mistakes into better clinical reasoning.

cards.title: Closed-Loop Communication
cards.body: In emergencies and team procedures, miscommunication can be life-threatening. Closed-loop communication ensures every critical instruction is received, understood, and confirmed.

bullets.label: This technique is particularly essential during
bullets.text: This technique is particularly essential during rapid deterioration events, medication administration, and high-risk handovers — forming a cornerstone of NCLEX-aligned safe practice.

bullets.label: Never rely on family members to interpret clinical information — use accredited interpreter services.
Adapt explanations to the individual's level of understanding. Avoid jargon; use plain language and teach-back methods.
Explore cultural preferences and values. Assumptions can compromise trust, consent, and patient safety.

cards.title: Professional Documentation Standards
cards.body: What to Record After Any Procedure

bullets.label: What was done and what was found
Any adverse events and immediate action taken

cards.title: Clinical Handover
cards.body: Handover is a high-risk moment in every clinical shift. Effective handover makes current risks and required actions immediately clear to the receiving team.

bullets.label: During a simulated deterioration station, the
bullets.text: During a simulated deterioration station, the nurse identifies low oxygen saturation, activates the emergency response, delegates tasks clearly, and repeats critical instructions using closed-loop communication.

bullets.label: The team performed well clinically — however,
bullets.text: The team performed well clinically — however, debriefing revealed that documentation of the deterioration response was incomplete. A key NCLEX learning point: documentation is part of the care, not an afterthought.

bullets.label: Use simulation to develop both technical skill and clinical judgement
Close the loop on all critical communications — especially in emergencies
Tailor explanations to culture, language, and health literacy level
Record complications, responses, and follow-up — every time, without exception
